title: K-flat normalization and coefficient coherence of the finite derived comparison
statement:
Let $u:(\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal D),S)\to(\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal C),R)$ be a morphism of ringed topoi presented by small sites, with commutative coefficient rings [def-weil-pbc-ringed-topos-morphism]. Use unbounded derived categories of module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-weil-abstract-derived-category], K-flat complexes with flat terms [def-pc-kflat-complex, def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules], and signed direct-sum total tensor [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves]. Write $F=Lu^*$ and $T_R,T_S$ for the K-flat derived pullback and tensor functors [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback].

The canonical natural comparison $\nu:F T_R\xrightarrow{\sim}T_S(F,F)$ has the following simultaneous representative normalization. For every flat-term K-flat pair $P,Q$, the total tensor $\operatorname{Tot}(P\otimes_R Q)$ and its pullback are flat-term K-flat, and the representative of $\nu$ under the canonical derived-functor comparison maps is the localized chain isomorphism
$$c_{u;P,Q}:u^*\operatorname{Tot}(P\otimes_RQ)\longrightarrow\operatorname{Tot}(u^*P\otimes_Su^*Q),\quad s\otimes(x\otimes y)\longmapsto(s\otimes x)\otimes(1\otimes y).$$
Its inverse has formula $(s\otimes x)\otimes(t\otimes y)\mapsto st\otimes(x\otimes y)$. This normalization is natural for arbitrary derived morphisms and independent of the chosen resolutions, and identifies this localized map with the canonical ringed-topos tensor comparison.

The comparisons satisfy the associativity, action-unit, and Koszul symmetry equations, with sign $(-1)^{pq}$ on degrees $(p,q)$. For every composable ringed-topos morphism $v$ the canonical pullback compositor $a:F_{u\circ v}\cong F_vF_u$ satisfies
$$(a_M\otimes a_N)\nu_{u\circ v;M,N}=\nu_{v;F_uM,F_uN}\,F_v(\nu_{u;M,N})\,a_{T_R(M,N)}.$$
For coefficient maps $R\to R'$, $S\to S'$ and $u^{-1}R'\to S'$ making the structural ring square commute, put $E_R=-\otimes_R^LR'$, $E_S=-\otimes_S^LS'$, and $F'=Lu'^*$. Let $\varepsilon_R:E_RT_R\cong T_{R'}(E_R,E_R)$ and $\varepsilon_S$ be the canonical derived scalar tensor comparisons, and $\kappa:F'E_R\cong E_SF$ the scalar-association comparison. Then the following equality holds for every $M,N\in D(R)$:
$$(\kappa_M\otimes\kappa_N)\nu'_{E_RM,E_RN}\,F'(\varepsilon_{R;M,N})=\varepsilon_{S;FM,FN}\,E_S(\nu_{M,N})\,\kappa_{T_R(M,N)}.$$
All maps in this square are normalized by their ordinary balanced chain maps on flat-term K-flat representatives. The equations hold for identity changes and successive changes of coefficients and in particular for quotient changes; neither a boundedness assumption nor flatness of the coefficient maps is required.

proof.text: Put $V=\operatorname{Tot}(P\otimes_RQ)$. By [lem-pur-kflat-total-tensor-model], $V$ is K-flat with flat terms, even for complexes unbounded in both directions. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topos-kflat-pullback] to $P,Q,V$: their termwise pullbacks are K-flat with flat terms. Thus $V$ computes the source derived tensor and $u^*V$ computes its derived pullback, while the target total tensor computes the tensor of the two derived pullbacks. All sites and ring sheaves meet the small-site and commutativity hypotheses of these two lemmas.

proof.text: On flat-term K-flat representatives, use the universal pullback computation [lem-weil-pbc-pullback-resolving-computation]. Flat-term K-flat resolutions [lem-pc-kflat-resolution], transported from the native tensor-flat predicate by [lem-weil-pbc-independent-sheaf-tensor-colimits], and fully faithful restriction [lem-pur-derived-resolving-pair-restriction] give fully faithful restriction of bifunctor categories. Restrict the supplied site tensor models and uncurry the natural cochain comparison of [lem-weil-pbc-cochain-pullback-tensor-shift]. The tensor-comparison representative descent theorem [lem-weil-pbc-tensor-comparison-descent-representatives] then gives a unique natural isomorphism with exactly the displayed normalized square. Proof irrelevance identifies the existential resolving witnesses in the uniqueness implication. The cochain comparison is the inverse of scalar contraction, so the chosen map retains the prescribed insertion-of-one formula. The uncurried comparison, its component equation and the total-tensor map equation are the extracted, fully proved native API in lem-pur-finite-tensor-comparison-proof-support.
